description: Portable decision policy for adaptive Ask vs Act behavior across all agent runtimes

act_immediately.description: Known decisions that can be made autonomously without interrupting user flow
conditions: Answer is explicitly stated in PRD or user instructions
Answer is defined in repository configuration or established conventions
Answer follows verified project patterns and rules
Action is reversible, safe, and within approved task scope
examples: File naming convention (defined in coding rules)
Module structure pattern (defined in architecture rules)
Test file location (defined in testing skill)

infer_and_act.description: High-confidence technical inferences from available context
conditions: PRD implies the technical choice with high confidence
Existing codebase patterns clearly dictate the convention
Tech stack constraints limit options to one viable choice
Standard software engineering best practice strongly favors one option
examples: Database schema structure aligning with existing data model
Multi-tenancy isolation pattern matching existing tenant queries
HTTP status codes and error envelope schema consistency
Cache key conventions matching existing Redis patterns
infer_and_act.requirement: Record the inference in .ai/state/decisions.json with confidence score and rationale

research_first.description: Uncertain technical details that can be resolved via inspection or docs without user disruption
conditions: Answer can be determined by reading existing code or dependency versions
Behavior depends on installed library API contracts
examples: Best pagination strategy for a specific query pattern
Whether an installed library supports a required feature
Performance implications of a query design

ask_user.description: Genuinely ambiguous business requirements or high-blast-radius decisions requiring user choice
conditions: Requirement has multiple conflicting business interpretations
High-risk architectural decision with irreversible consequences
Production deployment or external service publishing
Business logic decision that cannot be inferred from technical context
examples: User role permissions hierarchy when not defined in PRD
Pricing model or billing tier definitions
Dropping legacy database tables or deleting production resources
Choice between incompatible third-party SaaS vendors
ask_user.format: Formulate concise, numbered options with trade-offs and an engineering recommendation
